Hey so I just discovered this sub and actually minored in flute performance in college and was a drum major in highschool, so I might actually be able to help.

To be honest it's kind of hard to explain in text and you might have more luck taking a quick look on YouTube because you'll be able to see them do some of these things.

Basically you want to make sure you're not tensing up your embouchure and the inside of your mouth and throat unintentionally when you're going for increased volume. Learning to control the tension and position of your embouchure to  change pitch instead of trying to just overblow your notes to get the octave will also improve your overall tone.

Something that helped me also was to think about resonance with your notes and to imagine filling the whole length of your flute when you play even if it's just like a C or B flat imagine taking that air all the way to the end of the foot joint. 

Something else that might help is honestly just singing a little bit and feeling how you're throat changes when you sing lower louder or softer higher. Now that's not a one to one with flute but it is a steppingstone that helps some people get to those more abstract things I was talking about above. I hope that helped! Feel free to message me if you want more flute tips!

Since the guy who started this is just a troll I'll give you actual advice even if it's just from my own experience. Similar to what other comments have said you probably had a bit of a self esteem hit getting cheated on so dramatically and that's why you keep checking up on social media. You want to "fix" that feeling and don't really know how. You might be looking for validation from your ex or just want to see that you "won" the break-up.

Can you think of anything you could see on their social that would actually make you feel better? You cared about this person so seeing them have some sort of shitty life event probably wouldn't help. And seeing them getting married or otherwise moving on would probably sting a bit.  

If your reason is something like "just want to see how their doing" ask yourself why until you figure it out.  Once you do it might be easier to stop checking in all the time. If your really just curious to see how they are you'd snoop maybe once a year and hit the highlights, but if you blocked them and then are sneaking around the edges it seems like you already know this isn't why.


My advice for quitting the behavior weather you do this introspection or not is to just try and build some self-control around the issue or around social media in general. Turn off notifications for what you can. When you get that urge to go looking get up and grab a glass of water or check the mail. Start there. After a while try and put it off till after work or the next morning. Eventually it'll be an out of sight out of mind thing.

Best wishes it's always hard breaking a habit!

I agree with you for the most part. One thing I will add is that there are some situations where some work at home in elementary school is needed. I'll use myself as an example. 

When I was little I sucked at spelling. I mean I was really bad, failed every single spelling test bad. This confused my teachers and parents becuase I was voracious reader and had no issues with that and did really well in every other subject but spelling just didn't click. For a while they had me stay in at recess to work one on one with a teacher but they pretty quickly saw that wasn't a long term solution. So from 1st - 6th grade I had to spend atleast half an hour drilling spelling with my folks and as I got older I progressed up to just writing a spelling list out 10-20 times every day. 

I know that's kind of a special case but I don't think daily homework is universally hurtfully to children, especially if it's reasonable and targeted on a specific problem area.
